content: send <id|0xhash> "<text>" [-a] [-e] [-t] [-l] -a=ack  -e=encrypt(hash only)  -t=team plane; plain send=global/home (fails if no home)
-l = attach this node's position to THIS message. REFUSED unless the DM is SEALED (use -e, or `cfg set e2e_dm 1`),
refused if this node has no fix (set lat/lon), and refused as too_large if the +6 B no longer fits.
Replaces the removed `cfg set loc_dm`, which aired coordinates in the clear.
send_channel <ch> "<text>" [-t] [-g] [-e] [-l]   -t=team plane  -g=explicit global  `-t -g`=BOTH  plain=global
-e = seal the post to the TEAM content key. Valid ONLY as `-t -e`: a global channel has no key, and
`-t -g -e` is refused because the global copy would air the same text in the clear. With a key held,
`-t` seals by DEFAULT (`cfg set team_channel_crypt 0` opts out).  No -a on this verb.
-l = attach this node's position INSIDE the seal. `-t -l -e` sends text AND position in one sealed post.
REFUSED whenever the post would not actually be sealed (no team, no key, crypt off, or `-t -g`),
and refused `no_location` with no fix. Max text 173 B sealed, 167 B with -l.
send_layer <0xhash> <l1,l2,â¦> "<text>" [-a] [-e]   explicit cross-layer destination path; -e=encrypt (sealed relay); -l is refused (cross-layer carries no position)
whoami | lookup 0x<hash> | hashof <id> [-t|-s] | nameof 0x<hash> | resolve 0x<hash> [hard]   (hashes are 0x-prefixed; hashof prints 0xâ¦)
hashof searches BOTH id planes (static node_id and team local id) and NAMES the one that matched;
-t/-s narrow it. One number can legitimately answer in both â then both lines print.
peers | peers all    the address book: known peers (hash, name, static/team id, key confidence).
plain = the 16 rows we hold a key for (also the JSON book over BLE); `all` adds id-only rows (console only).
peerkey <ed_pub hex64> ["<name>"]   pin a scanned/QR pubkey (optional one-shot label, max 32)
peername 0x<hash> "<name>"  rename a CACHED peer (key + confidence untouched; works on a pinned peer)
reqpubkey <0xhash|id> [-t|-s]  request a peer's key on-air. A bare id searches BOTH planes (-t/-s force one).
If the id has no binding yet, it floods a BY-ID query ("who owns id N?"); the owner's answer is a CLAIM,
so run `reqpubkey <id>` once more afterwards to fetch the key itself. `hashof <id>` shows what landed.
mobile register [freq=<MHz> sf=<5-12> bw=<kHz> | scan]     arm registration: current PHY / a given PHY / scan known networks
mobile gateways            list learned gateways + networks
mobile query <gw>          pull a gateway's network directory
mobile status              attachment + home link + confirmation age + PHY
mobile unregister          end the attachment session -> dormant (no wire message)
team new                   mint a team (become its creator) â ALWAYS also mints its X25519 channel key
team <id> | team 0         join an existing team / leave (a join mints NO key â receive it by grant or QR)
[tkpub=<64 hex> tkpriv=<64 hex>]   adopt an EXISTING team channel keypair instead of minting (QR onboarding)
team exportkey             print this team's channel keypair as JSON (the app's team QR) â â  discloses a PRIVATE key
team grantkey <0xhash|team-id> [name="<text>"] [-t]   send this team's channel key to a teammate in a SEALED DM
needs a VERIFIED pubkey for the target (`reqpubkey <0xhash>` or a QR import) â never sent in the clear
pull_inbox <dm_since> <chan_since> | mark_read <dm|chan> <seq>       NDJSON out
del_msg <dm|chan> <seq>                     delete one record (erased|not_found|io_error)
clear_inbox confirm                         WIPE both stores (inbox ONLY; keeps everything else)
ui preset list                                 all 17 records incl. DISABLED, then ui_presets_end
ui preset set <emergency|dmN|channelN> loc=<on|off> "<text>"   text = 1..17 printable ASCII, no " \ CR LF
ui preset clear <dmN|channelN> | ui preset reset <emergency|dmN|channelN|all>   N=1..8; clear emergency -> mandatory
a mutating verb answers with the RESULTING record (`reset all`: the full list), or
{"ev":"ui_preset_err","reason":"bad_slot|bad_text|bad_location|mandatory|busy|store"}.
While an emergency is ACTIVE every mutating verb answers `busy` â including a no-op: an alarm's
retry series must never have its body or its location policy changed halfway through.
routes | status | duty | limits | cfg | cfg set <k> <v>
sleep [on|off] | debug [on|off] | regen | reboot | ota
version            build/git/board + last reset (no reset)
faults             the flash fault ring
crashtest <hang|fault|reboot>      (needs `debug on`)
rcmd <dst> <verb>      remote command via DM. status/routes = OPEN (cleartext); everything else = SEALED (needs `unlock`)
prep-restart       clear routes+inbox, KEEP join, go DORMANT (run fleet-wide, then power-cycle)
password <pass>        LOCAL-only: pin the fleet admin pubkey (derive from the passphrase) â set on every node
unlock <pass> | lock   operator device: derive the admin key into RAM to sign `rcmd`s / wipe it
then: `rcmd <dst> reboot` (etc.) is sealed to <dst>; `reqpubkey 0x<hash>` first if the target's pubkey isn't cached
route add <dest> <next_hop> <hops> [score_q4] | route del <dest>
testsend <dst> <run> [-a] [-e] -t ms1,ms2,â¦ | testch <ch> <run> -t ms1,ms2,â¦ | teststatus | testclear
factory_reset confirm      WIPE all flash (config+identity+peers+inbox) -> factory reboot
create layer= freq= bw= sf= sf_list= duty= name="<n>" [active_fraction=] [ch_min_ms=] [dm_min_ms=]
join layer= freq= bw= sf=      |  leave              layer=1..255 network id (leaf = layer & 0x0F)
gateway l0=<layer>:<node>:<ctrl_sf>:<data_sfs> l1=â¦  [period=] [win0=ms:off] [win1=] [beacon=] [freq0=] [freq1=] [bw0=] [bw1=] [cr0=] [cr1=] [gateway_only=]
dual-layer -> NV, reboot to apply.  e.g. gateway l0=1:1:8:7,9 l1=2:1:9:9,10
node_id name freq routing_sf bw cr tx_power sf_list lbt beacon_ms duty nav nav_ignore hop_cap team_hop_cap leaf_id
RF envelope on this board: freq 100..1000 MHz; tx_power -9..22 dBm nominal conducted
mobile mobile_autoregister host_mobiles intra_layer_relay gateway_only
lat lon e2e_dm team_channel_crypt intro_attach ble_mode ble_period ble_pin gw_announce_pct gw_announce_interval gw_herd_slack
active_fraction ch_min_ms dm_min_ms leaf_name
`name`=node identity Â· `leaf_name`=managed leaf (bumps epoch) Â· identity via `regen` Â· NO team_id key -> `team new`/`team <id>`/`team 0`
gateway-only keys: n_layers layer0_id window_period_ms l0_window_ms l0_window_offset_ms l1_layer_id l1_node_id l1_routing_sf l1_sf_list l1_beacon_ms l1_window_ms l1_window_offset_ms l1_freq
headings: UI PRESETS   (the OLED compose catalog: 17 stable slots â 1 emergency + 8 dm + 8 channel; NDJSON out)

content: send <id|0xhash> "<text>" [-a] [-e] [-t] [-l] -a=ack  -e=encrypt(hash only)  -t=team plane; plain send=global/home (fails if no home)
-l = attach this node's position to THIS message. REFUSED unless the DM is SEALED (use -e, or `cfg set e2e_dm 1`),
refused if this node has no fix (set lat/lon), and refused as too_large if the +6 B no longer fits.
Replaces the removed `cfg set loc_dm`, which aired coordinates in the clear.
send_channel <ch> "<text>" [-t] [-g] [-e] [-l]   -t=team plane  -g=explicit global  `-t -g`=BOTH  plain=global
-e = seal the post to the TEAM content key. Valid ONLY as `-t -e`: a global channel has no key, and
`-t -g -e` is refused because the global copy would air the same text in the clear. With a key held,
`-t` seals by DEFAULT (`cfg set team_channel_crypt 0` opts out).  No -a on this verb.
-l = attach this node's position INSIDE the seal. `-t -l -e` sends text AND position in one sealed post.
REFUSED whenever the post would not actually be sealed (no team, no key, crypt off, or `-t -g`),
and refused `no_location` with no fix. Max text 173 B sealed, 167 B with -l.
send_layer <0xhash> <l1,l2,â¦> "<text>" [-a] [-e]   explicit cross-layer destination path; -e=encrypt (sealed relay); -l is refused (cross-layer carries no position)
whoami | lookup 0x<hash> | hashof <id> [-t|-s] | nameof 0x<hash> | resolve 0x<hash> [hard]   (hashes are 0x-prefixed; hashof prints 0xâ¦)
hashof searches BOTH id planes (static node_id and team local id) and NAMES the one that matched;
-t/-s narrow it. One number can legitimately answer in both â then both lines print.
peers | peers all    the address book: known peers (hash, name, static/team id, key confidence).
plain = the 16 rows we hold a key for (also the JSON book over BLE); `all` adds id-only rows (console only).
peerkey <ed_pub hex64> ["<name>"]   pin a scanned/QR pubkey (optional one-shot label, max 32)
peername 0x<hash> "<name>"  rename a CACHED peer (key + confidence untouched; works on a pinned peer)
reqpubkey <0xhash|id> [-t|-s]  request a peer's key on-air. A bare id searches BOTH planes (-t/-s force one).
If the id has no binding yet, it floods a BY-ID query ("who owns id N?"); the owner's answer is a CLAIM,
so run `reqpubkey <id>` once more afterwards to fetch the key itself. `hashof <id>` shows what landed.

mobile gateways            list learned gateways + networks
mobile query <gw>          pull a gateway's network directory
mobile status              attachment + home link + confirmation age + PHY
mobile unregister          end the attachment session -> dormant (no wire message)
team new                   mint a team (become its creator) â ALWAYS also mints its X25519 channel key
team <id> | team 0         join an existing team / leave (a join mints NO key â receive it by grant or QR)
[tkpub=<64 hex> tkpriv=<64 hex>]   adopt an EXISTING team channel keypair instead of minting (QR onboarding)
team exportkey             print this team's channel keypair as JSON (the app's team QR) â â  discloses a PRIVATE key
team grantkey <0xhash|team-id> [name="<text>"] [-t]   send this team's channel key to a teammate in a SEALED DM
needs a VERIFIED pubkey for the target (`reqpubkey <0xhash>` or a QR import) â never sent in the clear

ui preset set <emergency|dmN|channelN> loc=<on|off> "<text>"   text = 1..17 printable ASCII, no " \ CR LF
ui preset clear <dmN|channelN> | ui preset reset <emergency|dmN|channelN|all>   N=1..8; clear emergency -> mandatory
a mutating verb answers with the RESULTING record (`reset all`: the full list), or
{"ev":"ui_preset_err","reason":"bad_slot|bad_text|bad_location|mandatory|busy|store"}.
While an emergency is ACTIVE every mutating verb answers `busy` â including a no-op: an alarm's
retry series must never have its body or its location policy changed halfway through.
